blocks.explanation:
A proper fraction with a repeated irreducible quadratic factor \((x^2 + 2)^2\) and a linear factor: Case IV.
We must find five constants.
Plan: put \(x = 2\), compare coefficients one power at a time, test with the constants, recombine.
steps:
Given: \(\frac{2x - 5}{(x^2 + 2)^2(x - 2)}\).
To find: its partial fractions.
Method: Degree 1 < degree 5, so it is proper. \(x^2 + 2\) cannot be factorised (\(x^2 = -2\) is impossible) and it is repeated: Case IV. Put \(x = 2\) for \(A\), then compare the coefficients of \(x^4, x^3, x^2, x\) for \(B, C, D, E\).

Write the partial fractions
\[\dfrac{2x - 5}{(x^2 + 2)^2(x - 2)}\]
\[= \dfrac{A}{x - 2} + \dfrac{Bx + C}{x^2 + 2}\]
\[+ \dfrac{Dx + E}{(x^2 + 2)^2}\]
Why: The repeated irreducible quadratic \((x^2 + 2)^2\) needs one fraction for each power, each with a linear top (Case IV).

Clear the denominators: the identity
\[2x - 5 = A(x^2 + 2)^2\]
\[+ (Bx + C)(x^2 + 2)(x - 2)\]
\[+ (Dx + E)(x - 2) \quad \text{(i)}\]
Why: Multiply both sides by \((x^2 + 2)^2(x - 2)\); each top keeps the factors not under it.

Put \(x = 2\) in (i) to find \(A\)
\[4 - 5 = A(4 + 2)^2 + 0 + 0\]
\[-1 = 36A\]
\[A = -\dfrac{1}{36}\]
Why: \(x = 2\) makes \(x - 2 = 0\), so the \(B, C, D, E\) terms all vanish.

Expand each part of (i)
\[A(x^2 + 2)^2 = Ax^4 + 4Ax^2 + 4A\]
\[(x^2 + 2)(x - 2)\]
\[= x^3 - 2x^2 + 2x - 4\]
\[(Bx + C)(x^3 - 2x^2 + 2x - 4)\]
\[= Bx^4 + (C - 2B)x^3\]
\[+ (2B - 2C)x^2 + (2C - 4B)x - 4C\]
\[(Dx + E)(x - 2)\]
\[= Dx^2 + (E - 2D)x - 2E\]
Why: Every product is multiplied out so that each power of \(x\) can be collected.

Group by powers of \(x\)
\[x^4:\ A + B\]
\[x^3:\ C - 2B\]
\[x^2:\ 4A + 2B - 2C + D\]
\[x:\ -4B + 2C - 2D + E\]
\[\text{const}:\ 4A - 4C - 2E\]
Why: These are the coefficients of the right side of (i); the left side \(2x - 5\) has \(x\)-coefficient 2, constant \(-5\) and 0 for the other powers.

Compare the \(x^4\) and \(x^3\) coefficients
\[0 = A + B\]
\[B = -A = \dfrac{1}{36}\]
\[0 = C - 2B\]
\[C = 2B = \dfrac{2}{36} = \dfrac{1}{18}\]
Why: There is no \(x^4\) or \(x^3\) on the left, so both coefficients are 0.

Compare the \(x^2\) coefficients
\[0 = 4A + 2B - 2C + D\]
\[D = -4A - 2B + 2C\]
\[= \dfrac{4}{36} - \dfrac{2}{36} + \dfrac{4}{36}\]
\[= \dfrac{6}{36} = \dfrac{1}{6}\]
Why: No \(x^2\) on the left; put in \(A = -\frac{1}{36}\), \(B = \frac{1}{36}\), \(C = \frac{2}{36}\).

Compare the \(x\) coefficients
\[2 = -4B + 2C - 2D + E\]
\[E = 2 + 4B - 2C + 2D\]
\[= 2 + \dfrac{4}{36} - \dfrac{4}{36} + \dfrac{1}{3}\]
\[= \dfrac{7}{3}\]
Why: On the left the coefficient of \(x\) is 2. Note \(2D = \frac{1}{3}\).

Test with the constants
\[4A - 4C - 2E\]
\[= -\dfrac{4}{36} - \dfrac{8}{36} - \dfrac{14}{3}\]
\[= -\dfrac{1}{3} - \dfrac{14}{3} = -5 \;\checkmark\]
Why: The constant equation was not used; it gives \(-5\), the constant on the left.

Write the partial fractions
\[Bx + C = \dfrac{x}{36} + \dfrac{2}{36} = \dfrac{x + 2}{36}\]
\[Dx + E = \dfrac{x}{6} + \dfrac{14}{6} = \dfrac{x + 14}{6}\]
Why: Write \(E = \frac{7}{3} = \frac{14}{6}\) so that \(D\) and \(E\) share the denominator 6; the numbers 36 and 6 move into the denominators.

Check: recombine
Common denominator \(36(x^2 + 2)^2(x - 2)\); top:
\[-(x^2 + 2)^2 = -x^4 - 4x^2 - 4\]
\[(x + 2)(x - 2)(x^2 + 2)\]
\[= x^4 - 2x^2 - 8\]
\[6(x + 14)(x - 2)\]
\[= 6x^2 + 72x - 168\]
\[\text{Top} = 72x - 180\]
\[= 36(2x - 5) \;\checkmark\]
Why: Over the common denominator \(36(x^2 + 2)^2(x - 2)\) the top is \(36(2x - 5)\); cancelling 36 gives back the question.

blocks.text: The answer key prints this answer under a second label "3" (the Exercise 5.2 key is labelled 1, 2, 3, 6, 7, 3). The answer itself, \(\frac{-1}{36(x - 2)} + \frac{x + 2}{36(x^2 + 2)} + \frac{x + 14}{6(x^2 + 2)^2}\), is correct.
